title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific `target` number.

Return the 0-based indices of the two numbers as a two-element array `[index1, index2]`. You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you cannot use the same element twice.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

examples.explanation: The sum of 2 and 7 is 9. Therefore index1 = 0, index2 = 1.
The sum of 2 and 4 is 6. Therefore index1 = 0, index2 = 2.

editorial.approach: Use the two-pointer approach. Set left = 0 and right = n - 1. Calculate sum = nums[left] + nums[right]. If sum === target, return [left, right]. If sum < target, increment left. If sum > target, decrement right.

hints: Since the array is sorted, you can check values from both ends to narrow down the target.
If their sum matches target, return their indices. If the sum is too small, increment `left`. If the sum is too large, decrement `right`.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Use nested loops to check every pair of elements in the array to see if they sum up to target.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use the two-pointer technique to search from both ends inwards, shrinking the bounds in linear time and O(1) space.

interviewExplanation: A brute-force solution checks all pairs in O(n^2) time. While we can use a hash map for O(n) time and O(n) space, the fact that the array is sorted allows us to use a two-pointer approach, optimizing the space complexity to O(1).
